text:
## Common Mistakes (Don't Make These!)  
❌ **Mistake 1:** Opening account without seeing original ID
✅ **Correct:** Always verify original, then copy  
❌ **Mistake 2:** Accepting address proof dated >3 months ago
✅ **Correct:** Require current document within 3 months  
❌ **Mistake 3:** Relying on verbal description instead of documentation
✅ **Correct:** Require documentation for every verification  
❌ **Mistake 4:** Skipping KYC because customer is "nice"
✅ **Correct:** KYC applies to EVERY customer, no exceptions

raw_entities.description: The process of verifying a customer's identity by examining original identification documents before account opening. This is a mandatory step that cannot be bypassed regardless of customer relationship or perceived trustworthiness.
context: Opening account without seeing original ID

raw_entities.name: Address Verification
raw_entities.description: The process of verifying a customer's address using current documentation. Address proof must be dated within the last 3 months and cannot be older than this threshold.
context: Accepting address proof dated >3 months ago

raw_entities.name: Universal KYC Application
raw_entities.description: A compliance obligation requiring that Know Your Customer procedures be applied to every customer without exception, regardless of customer relationship status, perceived trustworthiness, or other subjective factors.
context: KYC applies to EVERY customer, no exceptions

raw_entities.name: Documentation-Based Verification Requirement
raw_entities.description: A compliance obligation prohibiting reliance on verbal descriptions or customer statements for verification purposes. All verification must be supported by physical or documented evidence.
context: Relying on verbal description instead of documentation
